shortfall_bcf.label: sourced
shortfall_bcf.source: ADN editorial board, "The winter nobody wants to imagine", Aug 8, 2026: Enstar president John Sims says Enstar could enter the winter 3 Bcf short. https://www.adn.com/opinions/editorials/2026/08/08/editorial-the-winter-nobody-wants-to-imagine/

shortfall_days.label: sourced
shortfall_days.source: ADN editorial board, Aug 8, 2026: Sims described the 3 Bcf gap as the equivalent of 18 days with no heat in sustained cold. https://www.adn.com/opinions/editorials/2026/08/08/editorial-the-winter-nobody-wants-to-imagine/

storage_aug_bcf.label: sourced
storage_aug_bcf.source: ADN editorial board, Aug 8, 2026, citing the CINGSA public dashboard: ~6.54 Bcf in storage on Aug 7 (13 Bcf working capacity). https://www.adn.com/opinions/editorials/2026/08/08/editorial-the-winter-nobody-wants-to-imagine/

record_day_mmcf.label: sourced
record_day_mmcf.source: ADN (Alex DeMarban), Feb 2, 2024: Enstar delivered 268 MMcf/day around midnight Wed Jan 31, 2024, beating the 254 MMcf record of Jan 19, 2017. https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2024/02/02/southcentral-alaska-shatters-record-for-natural-gas-use-during-subzero-cold-streak/

jan_avg_mmcfd.label: sourced
jan_avg_mmcfd.source: ADN (Alex DeMarban), Feb 2, 2024: Enstar's average January throughput is about 160 MMcf/day (Sims). https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2024/02/02/southcentral-alaska-shatters-record-for-natural-gas-use-during-subzero-cold-streak/

jan2024_total_bcf.label: sourced
jan2024_total_bcf.source: ADN (Alex DeMarban), Feb 2, 2024: Enstar customers used 5.6 Bcf in January 2024 (Sims). https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2024/02/02/southcentral-alaska-shatters-record-for-natural-gas-use-during-subzero-cold-streak/

annual_bcf.label: sourced
annual_bcf.source: ADN / Alaska Journal of Commerce (Elwood Brehmer), May 14, 2020: Enstar expects demand to remain at roughly 33.6 Bcf/year through 2025 (a 2020 forecast). https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2020/05/14/new-natural-gas-deal-by-hilcorp-and-enstar-could-bring-rate-savings/

deliverability_loss_mmcfd.label: sourced
deliverability_loss_mmcfd.source: Enstar, "2024 Winter Update" slides to the House Special Committee on Energy, Feb 6, 2024: Jan 14 field order cut CINGSA withdrawal capacity from 150 to 121.5 MMcf/d (a Jan 25 order cut it further, to 105). https://www.akleg.gov/basis/get_documents.asp?session=33&docid=28450

needle_peak_mmcfd.label: sourced
needle_peak_mmcfd.source: Petroleum News (Alan Bailey), "New Enstar supplies", Mar 6, 2016: Hilcorp contract needle-peak call option, up to 20 MMcf/day extra in Dec–Feb. https://www.petroleumnews.com/pntruncate/978589605.shtml

marginal_price_usd_mcf.label: sourced
marginal_price_usd_mcf.source: ADN editorial board, Aug 8, 2026: HEX offered to sell gas to Enstar at $17.50 per Mcf, 30% above the $13.50 contract price. https://www.adn.com/opinions/editorials/2026/08/08/editorial-the-winter-nobody-wants-to-imagine/

avg_home_mcf_year.label: sourced
avg_home_mcf_year.source: ADN (Suzanna Caldwell), "Results are in for latest Southcentral Alaska Energy Watch drill", Nov 6, 2012: Enstar's John Sims, "The average home consumes 149 thousand cubic feet (mcf) of natural gas a year." Range across sources in docs/sources.md. https://www.adn.com/energy/article/results-are-latest-southcentral-alaska-energy-watch-drill/2012/11/06/

customers.label: sourced
customers.source: ADN (Alex DeMarban), Feb 2, 2024: Enstar's 150,000 customers; Enstar's Feb 6, 2024 legislative slides say 152,000. https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2024/02/02/southcentral-alaska-shatters-record-for-natural-gas-use-during-subzero-cold-streak/

lng_earliest.label: sourced
lng_earliest.source: Homer News (Jeffrey Kennett), Sep 10, 2026: Kenai Mayor Henry Knackstedt said Sims indicated a Nikiski import project may not be ready until Q4 2029. https://www.homernews.com/2026/09/10/winter-gas-shortfall-comes-into-sharper-focus-for-southcentral-alaska/

socal_event_pct.label: sourced
socal_event_pct.source: CALMAC SCG0224, "2018-2019 Winter Load Impact Evaluation of SoCalGas Smart Therm Program", Oct 24, 2019: 15.1% aggregate reduction in morning event hours. https://www.calmac.org/publications/SoCalGas_2019_DR_Evaluation_Report_-_PUBLIC_FINAL.pdf

socal_daily_pct.label: sourced
socal_daily_pct.source: CALMAC SCG0224, Oct 24, 2019: net daily savings on a morning-event day 0.207 MMcf, or 2.2%. https://www.calmac.org/publications/SoCalGas_2019_DR_Evaluation_Report_-_PUBLIC_FINAL.pdf

coned_snapback_pct.label: sourced
coned_snapback_pct.source: Con Edison, "Gas Demand Response Report on Pilot Performance – 2019/2020", Jul 1, 2020 (NY PSC Case 17-G-0606): snapback reduced calculated load reduction by an average of 52%; the 2020/2021 report repeats 52%. https://documents.dps.ny.gov/public/Common/ViewDoc.aspx?DocRefId=%7B7FA119BD-B04D-4378-95A3-BB26697815AC%7D

winter_optout_pct.label: sourced
winter_optout_pct.source: NRECA Business & Technology Report, "Shifting Space Conditioning Load: A Smart Thermostat Demand Response Pilot", Jun 2021 (electric co-op pilot): opt-outs of 13% (summer) and 6% (winter) of events. https://www.cooperative.com/programs-services/bts/Documents/Reports/Report-Smart-Thermostat-Pilot-June-2021.pdf

socal_cost_usd_therm.label: sourced
socal_cost_usd_therm.source: SoCalGas DR application A.23-01, Ch. 1 (Darren Hanway), Jan 6, 2023: proposed $15M pilots project an average levelized cost of $17.65/therm shifted or shed. https://www.socalgas.com/sites/default/files/2023-01/DR_Application_Chapter_1_Policy.pdf

rebate_upfront_usd.label: sourced
rebate_upfront_usd.source: SoCalGas press release, Dec 20, 2018: Smart Therm participants receive a $50 incentive. https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/socalgas-makes-energy-saving-this-winter-even-smarter-with-new-smart-therm-program-300769742.html

rebate_annual_usd.label: sourced
rebate_annual_usd.source: SoCalGas press release, Dec 20, 2018: an additional $25 for staying enrolled through the winter (to Apr 1, 2019). https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/socalgas-makes-energy-saving-this-winter-even-smarter-with-new-smart-therm-program-300769742.html

energy_watch_2012_pct.label: sourced
energy_watch_2012_pct.source: ADN (Suzanna Caldwell), Nov 6, 2012: the 2-hour Energy Watch drill on the evening of Oct 31, 2012 reduced the area's energy load by 1.5 percent. https://www.adn.com/energy/article/results-are-latest-southcentral-alaska-energy-watch-drill/2012/11/06/ Corroborated: Homer News, "Conservation drill cuts load by about 1.5 percent", Nov 15, 2012, https://www.homernews.com/2012/11/15/conservation-drill-cuts-load-by-about-1-5-percent/

hhv_btu_per_cf.label: sourced
hhv_btu_per_cf.source: EIA, "Heat Content of Natural Gas Delivered to Consumers" (released Sep 30, 2026), Alaska, 2025: 988 Btu/cf (2020–2025: 985, 982, 984, 998, 1,003, 988). https://www.eia.gov/dnav/ng/ng_cons_heat_a_epg0_vgth_btucf_a.htm

space_heat_share.label: assumed
space_heat_share.source: Assumed 0.75. Check: EIA RECS 2020, Alaska, natural gas use per household by end use (hundred cubic feet): space heating 969, water heating 336, clothes dryers 23, cooking 23, so space heating is 71.7–74.2% (RSE ~4%). https://www.eia.gov/consumption/residential/data/2020/state/pdf/ce5.4.st.pdf

eta_furnace.label: assumed
eta_furnace.source: Assumed 0.85 (AFUE, seasonal). Between the federal minimum for non-weatherized gas furnaces, 80% AFUE since Nov 19, 2015, and condensing furnaces (95% AFUE becomes the federal minimum on Dec 18, 2028). Federal Register, Dec 18, 2023, document 2023-25514 (DOE final rule, consumer furnaces): https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-12-18/html/2023-25514.htm . It cancels out of gas savings because UA is calibrated from gas use.

hdd_annual.label: derived
hdd_annual.source: Mean annual HDD 1996–2025, ANCHORAGE TED STEVENS INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (PANC), ACIS StnData; see data/calibration.json

ua_mean_btuh_per_f.label: derived
ua_mean_btuh_per_f.source: space_heat_share × avg_home_mcf_year × 1,000 × hhv_btu_per_cf × eta_furnace ÷ (24 × hdd_annual) = 0.75 × 149,000 × 988 × 0.85 ÷ (24 × 9818.5); see data/calibration.json

floor_min_f.label: assumed
floor_min_f.source: Design choice: hard minimum comfort floor

max_depth_default_f.label: assumed
max_depth_default_f.source: Design choice: default maximum setback depth

exempt_share.label: assumed
exempt_share.source: Share of enrolled homes exempt (infant, elderly, medical) (master plan §9)

tier2_effectiveness.label: assumed
tier2_effectiveness.source: Effectiveness of a Tier 2 pledged (manual) setback relative to automated Tier 1

override_rate.label: assumed
override_rate.source: Set equal to winter_optout_pct from the cooperative pilot; applying it to Anchorage is an assumption

validation_socal_daily_band.label: assumed
validation_socal_daily_band.source: Design choice: band around the published 2.2% (master plan §9)

headroom_2024_mmcfd.label: sourced
headroom_2024_mmcfd.source: ADN (Sean Maguire), "Enstar tells lawmakers it was 'extremely close' to being unable to deliver gas during Anchorage cold snap", Feb 6, 2024: on the record cold evening CINGSA was maxed out and Hilcorp could deliver only an additional 10 million cubic feet (Sims to the House Energy Committee). Approximate; the article gives no time unit, read here as per day. https://www.adn.com/business-economy/energy/2024/02/06/enstar-tells-lawmakers-gas-storage-was-extremely-close-to-being-depleted-during-recent-anchorage-cold-snap/

deliverability_2024_mmcfd.label: derived
deliverability_2024_mmcfd.source: feb2024 scenario's modeled peak gas day (268.0 MMcf, data/scenarios/feb2024.json) + headroom_2024_mmcfd (10)

linepack_usable_mmcf.label: derived
linepack_usable_mmcf.source: usableLinepackMMcf(deliverability_2024_mmcfd, demand_shape.json) in packages/model/src/pressure.ts: the smallest linepack that absorbs a normal day's hourly shape at 278 MMcf/day. Fixed; never recomputed from the deliverability slider

reserve_min_idx.label: assumed
reserve_min_idx.source: Covers differences between the hourly plan and the 5-minute simulation (AGENTS.md Section 6)

forecast_lag_h.label: assumed
forecast_lag_h.source: A forecast run is usable 1 h after its run time (AGENTS.md Section 6)

replan_interval_h.label: assumed
replan_interval_h.source: Matches the forecast issue cadence (AGENTS.md Section 6)

drift_temp_f.label: assumed
drift_temp_f.source: Drift trigger: observed minus forecast in use, sustained for drift_hours (AGENTS.md Section 6)

drift_hours.label: assumed
drift_hours.source: Consecutive hours over drift_temp_f before a drift re-plan (AGENTS.md Section 6)

drift_pressure_idx.label: assumed
drift_pressure_idx.source: Drift trigger: pressure index this far below what the plan expected (AGENTS.md Section 6)

drift_fade_h.label: assumed
drift_fade_h.source: A drift correction fades linearly to zero over this many hours (AGENTS.md Section 6)

demand_sensitivity_mmcfd_per_f.label: derived
demand_sensitivity_mmcfd_per_f.source: data/system_fit.json b: MMcf/day per heating degree day, i.e. per °F of daily mean. Shown as 3.44
